headlineClaims.evidence: recount 65503/65786; computed with B's unconstrained colour, A's colour is not fed to the decision. But the number is relative to B, and B's unconstrained road colour at weak scores is itself wrong often (audit sample: A right in 6/12 colour-mismatch-only pieces), so it is a lower bound on A-vs-B agreement, not an A error rate.
roads (49% of pieces) cannot disagree on kind in B (only 'none' above 95, never fired). Vertex-only kind agreement is 33741/33770 = 99.91%.
531 of them are the phantom-colour pieces (tautological), 28 are genuine. Of 12 genuine sampled: B right 4 (all the edge2168 e47 bronze road), A right 1, neither 4 (UI/robber), unclear 3.

186 of the 353 in inferred-seat games are pieces B strongly agrees with A on (score < 20, same colour), i.e. the seat inference is wrong, not A. Sample of 12: 4 real pieces with a missing inferred seat, 7 UI/no piece, 1 unclear. 0 of 178 phantom pieces in registry-seat games have strong B agreement, so registry seats look reliable.

40 of the 283 have B's seat-constrained colour equal to A. Sample of 12 non-phantom colour mismatches: A right 6 (white/silver, black/bronze, blue/black confusions in B at scores 55-70), B right 2, neither 2, unclear 2.
all 87 are inactive knights (61 level 1, 26 level 2), none phantom, worst score 14.9; 12/12 sampled are real knight badges A reported nothing for.
sample of 12: B right 3 (knight badges A read as settlements), neither 7 (trade cards / avatars / robber at the vertex), unclear 2, A right 0.

headlineClaims.verdict: confirmed as computed; says nothing about A
headlineClaims.evidence: the flag compares B's variant under A's colour with B's variant under B's colour. A carries no level/state; the report's A-side variant columns are B's templates.

headlineClaims.claim: UI overlays raise the mismatch rate ~60x; robber/merchant adjacency does not
headlineClaims.evidence: recount 164/1480 = 11.1% vs 119/64365 = 0.18%; robber 0.29% vs 0.45%; merchant 0.10% vs 0.46%. But roughly 45% of overlay-suspected captures are false positives (see overlay claim), so the 'with overlay' population is diluted.

headlineClaims.claim: bronze road A=180 vs B=59, 117 of A's on edge 5
headlineClaims.evidence: recount 180 / 117 / 59; edge 5 lies under the trade-offer panel (11 of 12 drop-candidate crops at e5 show the panel; 3 board views show the panel over tiles 2 and 6). All 59 B bronze roads are in games that seat bronze; 51 coincide with A, 8 are A=black roads at edge2168 e47 that are bronze by eye.

recount 2140/2152 (2143/2155), min margin 14.1; 10/10 random captures and 4/4 white3776 frames show the grey pawn inside the detected tile's robber circle. B's robber offset (-0.3, -0.26, 0.43 sp) differs from renderer.ts (-0.2, -0.05, 0.45) and B's is the one that matches real captures.

headlineClaims.claim: white3776 02-04 vertex 25 is caused by the black merchant moving to the tile below, not the robber
headlineClaims.evidence: board views: robber t16, t16, t17, t1 in frames 01-04; merchant t14 then t10 (below v25) from frame 02. A said mysticblue in frame 01 and white in 02-04; B says mysticblue in all four with byte-identical per-colour scores (16.2-16.3 vs white 30.6); registry seats mysticblue,gold,red,black. Whether the merchant caused A's flip is plausible but not provable from these data.

sample precision 4/12 on the flag as a whole; 3/12 in captures resting only on small ui-panel rectangles, 10/12 (+1 unclear) in captures with tokensFound<18, a hidden token >= 40 or a rectangle >= 1 spacing. The false positives are a number token welded to the white pasture sheep by the 16 px closing.

bugsAndLimitations.what: The flat-light-block test passes the white pasture sheep artwork; the two-block closing welds sheep + number token into a 0.6-0.8 spacing blob that clears the 0.45 spacing size filter. The comment 'Number tokens are far too small to pass' is true only for a token alone.
bugsAndLimitations.impact: about 45% of the 348 overlay-suspected captures and 617 of the 1482 under-overlay piece flags are false positives; mark-capture-overlay-contaminated is not safe as-is.

bugsAndLimitations.what: colour-mismatch-seat is set whenever the seat-constrained colour differs from A, which is automatic for every phantom-colour piece.
bugsAndLimitations.impact: the 559 headline is 531 phantom + 28 genuine; the flag adds no information for phantom pieces.

bugsAndLimitations.what: Seat inference needs a building and a road of the colour in at least two frames; games with two frames where A dropped one piece lose a seat.
bugsAndLimitations.impact: >= 186 false phantom-colour flags, 4/12 phantom samples were real pieces, 23 drop candidates are pieces B agrees with A on (one verified real: 20260912-spot2638/02 e15 black road).

bugsAndLimitations.what: B always returns the argmin colour for an edge; there is no 'nothing here' hypothesis below 95. At scores above ~45 the colour is close to arbitrary (white/silver, black/bronze, blue/black).
bugsAndLimitations.impact: colour-mismatch (283) overstates A's road errors; kind agreement on roads is structural; the seat-constrained colour should be preferred for roads.

bugsAndLimitations.what: Visible tokens score up to 24.8 (p99 13.7) and false hidden-token hits occur at 31.9 (king3990/01 t5) and 32.7 (ship4971/02 t3) on fully visible tokens; a true hit occurs at 27.9 (win9397/01 t15).
bugsAndLimitations.impact: hidden-token alone in the 25-40 band is unreliable; the rule contributed 8 sole-rule overlay flags.

bugsAndLimitations.what: A's metropolis type and knight level/state in the colour x variant table are taken from B's templates (A has neither).
bugsAndLimitations.impact: the A/B cells for those variants compare B with B on the variant axis; only the colour axis is an A-vs-B comparison.

bugsAndLimitations.what: The default run skips games whose registry status is 'watching'.
bugsAndLimitations.impact: 3 captures had no B result; added by this audit.

bugsAndLimitations.what: Not a B bug: the synthetic renderer draws the robber at (-0.2, -0.05) spacings, height 0.45; B's calibration on real captures (-0.3, -0.26, 0.43) is verified correct on 14 boards.
bugsAndLimitations.impact: training data places the robber lower and further right than the real game.
